cards.title: The central Sahel got wetter, 2000-2025
cards.headline: Across 48 one-degree land tiles (about 567,000 km²) in Central Sahel (Chad and eastern Niger), GLDAS-2.1 precipitation shows a detectable wetting trend of +48.5% per decade (+3.52 mm/month per decade, median tile, 2000-2025), with 100% of tiles significant after false-discovery correction.

robustness.detail: Selection criterion (regions are built from these tiles, so this passes by design): 48 of 48 tiles (100%) significant with the matching sign after Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery correction (q < 0.05).

Region trend (median over 48 tiles of OLS on annual means; overlapping windows) - 2000-2025: +48.4%/decade; 2003-2025: +50.0%/decade; 2000-2020: +37.5%/decade -> same sign, within a factor of 2. Global shares of significant land shrink in these windows (2003-2025: 1.3% wetting / 2.6% drying; 2000-2020: 0.7% wetting / 1.0% drying), but this region's trend keeps its sign and size.

robustness.check: Agreement between neighbour definitions (queen vs kNN LISA)
robustness.detail: Queen-contiguity LISA labels 100% of tiles as HH clusters; k-nearest-neighbour weights label 100% as HH, and 100% of the queen HH tiles keep their label under kNN.
1 source(s): 1 agree, 0 partly agree, 0 disagree.

user.who: An agricultural extension office in the central Sahel (e.g. a district extension team in Chad)
user.decision: Which millet and sorghum varieties and sowing windows to recommend to smallholders for the coming rainy season
user.why_it_matters: Advice built on the drought decades of the 1970s-80s may now be too conservative; a detectable wetting trend supports testing longer-cycle varieties, while year-to-year variability still argues for drought-hedged recommendations.

cards.evidence_level: robust pattern: passes all 3 extra checks (shorter windows, two neighbour definitions, literature)

literature.citation: Biasutti, M. (2019). Rainfall trends in the African Sahel: Characteristics, processes, and causes. WIREs Climate Change, 10(4), e591.
literature.note: Reviews the partial recovery of Sahel rainfall since the 1980s drought, stronger in the central/eastern Sahel.

caveats: Percent changes look large in arid places because the baseline is small; read the mm/month figure alongside the percentage.
Sahel rainfall recovery is partial and uneven; the western Sahel has recovered less than the centre.
A wetter seasonal total can co-occur with more intense, less frequent storms; totals alone do not describe planting risk.
GLDAS-2.1 precipitation is model forcing derived from GPCP; it is not an independent rain-gauge record.
Trends are statistical over 2000-2025; they shrink in shorter windows and do not identify causes.
Tile shares are after false-discovery correction; individual tiles can still be false positives.

user.who: A hydropower and water planner for the Biobío-to-Aysén river basins (Chile)
user.decision: How much water to allocate to irrigation and cities next season, and whether reservoir and desalination investments assume a drier baseline
user.why_it_matters: If the drying is a persistent trend rather than a run of bad years, water rights and reservoir rules that assume a return to 20th-century rainfall will over-allocate water.

literature.citation: Garreaud, R. D., Boisier, J. P., Rondanelli, R., Montecinos, A., Sepulveda, H. H., & Veloso-Aguila, D. (2020). The Central Chile Mega Drought (2010-2018): A climate dynamics perspective. International Journal of Climatology, 40(1), 421-439.

caveats: Only part of this cluster lies in the 30-38°S core of the central-Chile megadrought studied in the literature; most of it is south-central Chile and Patagonia.

cards.title: Paradox Earth caught a false trend
cards.headline: Paradox Earth caught a false trend: the apparent soil-water decline is a level shift around 2010-08 and 2024-07 that lines up with documented changes in the model's radiation input, not a trend, so it is withdrawn.

robustness.detail: Not graded: the series failed the homogeneity check first, so a trend p-value would be meaningless.

Level shift detected around 2010-08 and 2024-07. Soil water was the original headline: a 26-year global decline. Paradox Earth's own checks showed it is mostly two level shifts that follow documented changes in the radiation data driving the GLDAS model (a step in 2010-08 and a degraded period from 2024-07; GES DISC README_GLDAS2). Within the single consistent period 2012-01 to 2024-06 the global decline is not significant, so the trend was withdrawn and soil water is analysed only inside that window.
Not graded: a step change makes any window's slope depend on where the window sits relative to the break.

README_GLDAS2 documents an apparent shift in the AGRMET radiation climatology (section 1.5.3; detected here as a step at 2010-08) and degraded WWMCA radiation from mid-2024 (section 1.2.3; step at 2024-07). The 'trend' lines up with these documented input changes.

user.who: Teachers and students using the Paradox Earth explorer
user.decision: Whether to trust a dramatic trend line before checking how the data were made
user.why_it_matters: A tool that rejects its own most exciting result shows why every trend needs a homogeneity check, not just a p-value.

cards.evidence_level: withdrawn (data artefact caught by the detective)

literature.citation: NASA GES DISC. README Document for NASA GLDAS Version 2 Data Products (GLDAS-2.1 forcing section).
literature.note: States that the bias-correction scaling 'is unable to correct an apparent shift (of unknown origin) in the AGRMET climatology after 2011' for the radiation forcing.

literature.citation: Rodell, M., Houser, P. R., Jambor, U., et al. (2004). The Global Land Data Assimilation System. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 85(3), 381-394.
literature.note: Describes GLDAS as a model driven by changing observation-based forcing, which is why its outputs need homogeneity checks before trend analysis.

caveats: Withdrawn as a trend: the soil-water series is shown only as an example of a data artefact.
Precipitation (the variable we do report) comes from GPCP-based forcing and is checked for the same kind of break.
